facility_roles.note: ZEUS was built and operated at DESY on the HERA ring.
The HERA electron/positron and proton beams that ZEUS recorded were produced and accelerated at DESY.

physics_goals.quote: Measures neutral and charged current processes, as well as high energy photoproduction processes, in electron-proton and positron-proton interactions ... both inclusively and in exclusive channels, and searches for new interactions and new particles.
physics_goals.value: Measure neutral- and charged-current deep inelastic and photoproduction processes in e⁻p and e⁺p collisions, identify jets and leptons with precision tracking, and search for new interactions and particles

summary.plain: A particle detector at the German laboratory DESY, in Hamburg, that watched electrons and protons collide head-on to map out what a proton is made of, and to search for new particles and forces. It ran from 1992 until HERA, the collider it depended on, shut down on 30 June 2007.
summary.technical: General-purpose detector at one of the two collision points of the DESY HERA electron-proton collider (Hamburg, Germany); high-resolution compensating uranium-scintillator calorimeter, central tracking in a superconducting coil, silicon micro-vertex detector, forward/backward drift and straw-tube trackers, an instrumented iron muon absorber, and (from 2001) longitudinally polarized lepton beams. Operated 31 May 1992 to 30 June 2007.
